openwrt_wiki.seriell: -> [[docs:techref:hardware:port.serial]] general information about the serial port, serial port cable, etc. How to connect to the Serial Port of this specific device: The device uses TTL @ 3.3V and not a standard RS-232 Serial that operates between 3 and 15V, so **do not try to connect it to a common serial adapter: you will certainly fry the serial circuit** or even the whole board. There are plenty of USB to TTL and RS-232 to TTL available on the market, just be careful with the voltage: the standard is 5V and it may also damage your board. Look for the ones with 3.3V or with both voltages and a way to switch between them. Bits per second: **115200**\\ Data bits: **8**\\ Parity: **None**\\ Stop bits: **1**\\ Flow control: **None**\\ J1 PIN1: **3.3V**\\ PIN2: **GND**\\ PIN3: **RX**\\ PIN4: **TX**\\ PINS ----> Power On/Off / Wifi On/Off button side 4 3 2 1 <--- USB ports side
openwrt_wiki.installation: ==== Upgrade from ZyXEL customized OpenWrt ==== === Architecture and kernel size change from AR71xx to ATH79 notes === **Do not use Firmware OpenWrt Install unless you have modified the settings in the U-Boot loader** The ZyXEL factory firmware is based on the AR71xx architecture and has an older kernel, therefore the installation to 22.x (ATH79) needs to be performed in two steps, otherwise the device will end up in a boot loop and needs to be recovered with the factory software using tftp. Reason being the 22.x kernel is bigger and needs to be loaded in two steps. Firstly, install an AR71xx version, 19.07.10 [[https://archive.openwrt.org/releases/19.07.10/targets/ar71xx/generic/openwrt-19.07.10-ar71xx-generic-NBG6616-squashfs-factory.bin]] After the successful installation of 19.07.10 - you can connect to the router with ssh ssh root@192.168.1.1 This will allow you to access the U-Boot boot loader settings from within the ssh shell. (Doing this change from factory firmware is not possible) fw_setenv boot_openwrt bootm 0x9F120000 fw_setenv bootcmd run boot_openwrt After the settings are done, a sysupgrade can be performed to install the 22.x (ATH79) based OpenWrt. sysupgrade -F -n -v /tmp/openwrt-22.03.2-ath79-generic-zyxel_nbg6616-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin Reference: [[https://forum.openwrt.org/t/upgrade-zyxel-nbg6616-from-19-07-10-to-22-03-2-ar71xx-to-ath79/140486]] === Upgrade / installation procedure === On the ZyXEL firmware there is one large mtd partition for the kernel and everything. SSH into the router, user "root" and password (default is "1234"), and write the sysupgrade image to /dev/mtd6: # mtd -r write /tmp/firmware.bin /dev/mtd6 The following is a more detailed example of installing OpenWrt. ssh root@192.168.1.254 cd /tmp/ # the prompt should show root@nbg6161:/tmp wget http://downloads.openwrt.org/releases/18.06.2/targets/ar71xx/generic/openwrt-18.06.2-ar71xx-generic-NBG6616-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin -O firmware.bin mtd -r write /tmp/firmware.bin /dev/mtd6 Unlocking /dev/mtd6 ... Writing from /tmp/firmware.bin to /dev/mtd6 ... Rebooting ... [w] Now you can configure the device via ''%%http://192.168.1.1/%%'' ==== Sysupgrade ==== -> [[docs:guide-user:installation:generic.sysupgrade]] ==== Recovery ==== The device is able to flash from a tftp server. You can also abort the boot loader via serial if a cable is attached to a LAN port. * Configure your server to 192.168.1.33, netmask 255.255.255.0 * Attach to one of the LAN ports * Copy your firmware file into the tftp directory and name it ras.bin (IE download it from zyxel directly) * Next steps you have follow from this git [[commit>?p=openwrt/openwrt.git;a=commitdiff;h=459c8c9ef816156107e297964d088ddee2b4eef5]] * NBG6616 uboot is locked, so you have to unlock it first (follow steps in 2nd half of above git comment - after this paragraph "In order to escape/unlock a password challenge has to be passed.") * After you have unlocked your uboot you have set new variable (follow steps in 1st step of above git comment) * After you save your environment "saveenv" you can type "reset" to reboot your device * Turn on / restart device and holding down WPS key * Keep holding WPS key until the firmware is downloaded and router is flashing * Power cycle device when Power and USB2 LEDs flash. (It will take more than 5 minutes) ==== Technical note: header ==== Building an custom image that can be flashed currently requires adding a header. Either use genImgHdr from the open source bundle or implement a new header writer for OpenWrt (documentation is in the Makefile).

openwrt_git_ath79.hardwareteil_der_nachricht:
ath79: add support for ZyXEL NBG6616

Specifications:

  SoC: Qualcomm Atheros QCA9557
  RAM: 128 MB (Nanya NT5TU32M16EG-AC)
  Flash: 16 MB (Macronix MX25L12845EMI-10G)
  Ethernet: 5x 10/100/1000 (1x WAN, 4x LAN)
  Wireless: QCA9557 2.4GHz (nbg), QCA9882 5GHz (ac)
  USB: 2x USB 2.0 port
  Buttons: 1x Reset
  Switches: 1x Wifi
  LEDs: 11 (Pwr, WAN, 4x LAN, 2x Wifi, 2x USB, WPS)

MAC addresses:

WAN *:3f uboot-env ethaddr + 3
LAN *:3e uboot-env ethaddr + 2
2.4GHz *:3c uboot-env ethaddr
5GHz *:3d uboot-env ethaddr + 1

The label contains all four MAC addresses, however the one without
increment is first, so this one is taken for label MAC address.

Notes:

The Wifi is controlled by an on/off button, i.e. has to be implemented
by a switch (EV_SW). Despite, it appears that GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH needs
to be used, just like recently fixed for the NBG6716.
Both parameters have been wrong at ar71xx.

openwrt_image_mk.device:
define Device/zyxel_nbg6616
  SOC := qca9557
  DEVICE_VENDOR := Zyxel
  DEVICE_MODEL := NBG6616
  DEVICE_PACKAGES := kmod-usb2 kmod-usb-ledtrig-usbport kmod-rtc-pcf8563 \
	kmod-ath10k-ct ath10k-firmware-qca988x-ct
  IMAGE_SIZE := 15232k
  RAS_BOARD := NBG6616
  RAS_ROOTFS_SIZE := 14464k
  RAS_VERSION := "OpenWrt Linux-$(LINUX_VERSION)"
  IMAGES += factory.bin
  IMAGE/factory.bin := append-kernel | pad-to $$$$(BLOCKSIZE) | \
	append-rootfs | pad-rootfs | pad-to 64k | check-size | zyxel-ras-image
  SUPPORTED_DEVICES += nbg6616
endef

zyxel_spezifikation.green_tab:
Green - NBG6616 | ZyXEL
Detect cable length
The NBG6616 can detect the length of connected Ethernet cables and adjust power usage accordingly. The shorter the Ethernet cable length is, the less power it consumes.
Wireless output management
Easy to adjust the output power to reduce interference with neighboring access points within high wireless density areas.
Inactive Link Detection
Smartly adjusts power consumption by detecting the link status and the length of connected Ethernet cables. When the NBG6616 detects no active data transmission, the device automatically enters the power-saving mode to avoid energy waste.

led_abschaltbar.wert: per GPIO: power, usb1, usb2, wifi5g, wps; LAN/WAN-LEDs am Switch, 2.4-GHz-LED am WMAC

reset_knopf.wert: Rückseite; 1-4 s Neustart, über 5 s Werkseinstellungen

wps_knopf.wert: Front (Oberseite), GPIO 22; hält man ihn beim Einschalten, startet die TFTP-Recovery
wps_knopf.bemerkung: Lage laut Handbuch "front panel"; Recovery-Funktion laut OpenWrt-Commit/Wiki

knoepfe.wert: power switch, on/off switch, wifi switch, reset button

seriell_zugang.wert: innen Stiftleiste: bestückte 4-polige Stiftleiste zwischen 5-GHz-Abschirmung und den Schaltern; daneben unbestücktes 2x7-Lochfeld

seriell_pinbelegung.wert: J1: Pin 1 3.3V, Pin 2 GND, Pin 3 RX, Pin 4 TX; Reihenfolge laut Wiki-Skizze "4 3 2 1" mit Pfeilen Richtung Power-/WLAN-Schalter-Seite und USB-Seite
seriell_pinbelegung.bemerkung: Skizze im Wiki nicht eindeutig, Pin 1 vor dem Anschließen messen

seriell_hinweis.wert: Hersteller-Bootloader "ZyXEL zloader v2.02" über U-Boot; Eingriff in der Konsole ist gesperrt (Einzelheiten im Commit)

gluon_support.wert: Gluon ar71xx-generic als zyxel-nbg6616 (v2018.2 bis v2021.1.x, ATH10K_PACKAGES); in Gluon ath79-generic (v2022.1 bis main) nicht enthalten
Neanderfunk 2025.1: per eigenem targets-ath79-generic.patch als zyxel-nbg6616 (OpenWrt-Profil zyxel_nbg6616); USB-Geräteliste

installation.wert: Stock-Image ist ar71xx-basiert: erst OpenWrt 19.07.10 (ar71xx), dann U-Boot-Variablen anpassen, dann ath79-sysupgrade; sonst Bootloop. Recovery per TFTP (Server 192.168.1.33, Datei ras.bin, WPS beim Einschalten halten)
installation.bemerkung: Installationsmethoden laut hwdata: "CLI generic, see devicepage"; Recovery: "U-Boot TFTP recovery"

amazon_asin.bemerkung: amazon.de; aus den Amazon-Angebotslinks auf der Geizhals-Seite des NBG6616

geizhals_url.bemerkung: Artikel nennt nur NBG6616 (eine Hardware-Version bekannt)

offene_faeden.grund: 5-GHz-Testbericht (NII) nicht geladen: Leistung je Kanal, Antennenangaben 5 GHz
Hohlstecker-Maß und Polarität des DVE DSA-24PFD-15 FUS 120200 nicht lesbar; Datenblatt des Netzteils suchen
Wiki-Skizze J1 ("4 3 2 1" zwischen Schalter- und USB-Seite) nicht eindeutig; Foto media:zyxel:nbg6616_board.jpg nicht ausgewertet; Pin 1 am Gerät messen
EMG2826-Q10A / EMG2806-Q10A laut FCC baugleiche Marketingnamen: ob gleiche Platine/Firmware, nicht geprüft

lauf.notiz: ToH-Dump + Live-hwdata (2026-03-11), OpenWrt-Wiki (2024-02-12), Commits ar71xx/ath79, DTS/DTSI/generic.mk, Gluon-Targets (ar71xx bis v2021.1.x, nicht in ath79-generic; Neanderfunk-Patch), DeviWiki = WikiDevi, FCC I88NBG6616 (Grant, Label, Label-Ort, Handbuch, DTS-Testbericht, Aussen- und Innenfotos), Zyxel-Produkt- und Spezifikationsseite (Webarchiv 2014/2016), Geizhals-Archiv 2015 (EAN, ASIN). Widersprüche: Antennen "fixed" (Zyxel) vs. RSMA (FCC); Leistung 16.8 W (Label) vs. 24 W (Spezifikation); USB 1 (DeviWiki) vs. 2; RAM-Chip Wiki vs. Commit. Keine Werkstatt-Messung. Offen: DC-Stecker-Maß, J1-Pinlage am Gerät.

geizhals.ergebnis: Produktseite a1166955 per heise (1 Abruf), Datenblatt nach roh.geizhals, 14 Felder ergänzt; keine EAN/ASIN auf der Seite
